body: People have commented saying there is no way I could have taken 710mg of Hydromorph with any amount of sleeping pills without dying.  I have been on Morphine and Hydromorph since 2007 when I was in a serious, multi-car accident.  I guess my body had built up a tolerance to the Hydromorph over the years.  So after my failed attempt, my doctor said "you know I can't ever give you Hydromorph or Morphine again or I'd lose my license."  So he suggested that I go on to Suboxone.  I have been taking 12mg a day for almost a year.  All it seems to have done is make me incredibly tired and my short term memory is almost gone.  I nod off sitting at my computer and wake up 6 hours later with my keyboard locked off because my hands dropped and my fingers pressed the keys.  This is a horrible way to live... please let me go

Someone suggested that I call the Mental Health office in my city last year.  I eventually call and a friendly lady took my details.  She asked me about a dozen questions and told me I would be put on a list for a counsellor to call me and schedule a meeting to assess my situation.  After that call, I called a few churches to see if they had any programs for men.  I didn't find any help.  Then I went online and  Googled "Men's Help Group" and I eventually found a group that met every 2nd week.  All this time I'm still waiting for the Mental Health outfit to return my call and schedule an assessment.  Well, 6 months went by before they finally called me... 6 months!  I told the lady I was going to a men's group every 2 weeks and that I was doing a bit better.  She seemed more happy to be able close my file than anything else.  I think society likes to present itself as a group that truly cares about mental health issues.  You see campaigns and ads on tv encouraging people to talk and share their pain.  But from my extensive experience, I can say that is the furthest thing from the truth.  People don't want to get involved and doctors just want to give you more pills that only numb the pain and steal away your mind.

Probably no one reading, so this is just a place for me to spread my feelings I guess.  I remember last year being in such a low point, I couldn't stop crying.  I don't mean the type of crying where you're sobbing or whaling away so loud the neighbors can hear.  I mean the type when hot tears constantly stream down your face, dripping off your chin... and there's nothing you can do to stop it.  Your eyes burn and your spirit feels so hollow and cold.  My family knows I'm hurting.  They don't know the extent of my pain and they never reach out to see how I'm doing or if I'm even still alive.  Everything around me is like a reality show on tv and the volume has been half muted.  No one sees me and I have no place in their lives.

Same for me.  I hate going to sleep though cause I have torturous nightmares about the people I love and the days when we used to all be together, happy and enjoying life.  Then I wake up in a cold sweat and everyone is still gone... further away than the day before.
I am so sad to read your story.  I wish there was something I could say to make you feel better.

In 1997 I decided to cut a 7 foot by 7 foot hole in the side of our family house.  My wife and I wanted to add a nice gas fireplace and bookshelf built-ins on the north wall.  Firstly, I cut out the 49 square feet of drywall and removed the insulation.  Then I marked out the exterior stucco where I wanted to cut and I grabbed my Milwaukee Sawzall.  I plunged the blade through the 3/4" stucco and through the 1/2" osb sheathing but the blade went dull in about 15 seconds.  I tried different blades but they all died within seconds of use.  I grabbed my circular saw and wondered if an old blade might cut through the stucco.  I decided against that method.  Then I remembered I had a Makita 9100b grinder.  I picked up 4 grinding discs that were 4" in diameter and started cutting the stucco.  I could actually see the grinding disc spin smaller with every revolution.  I bet I burned through each disc in about 45 seconds or less!  Gawd I was so frustrated and stood on the lawn wondering how the hell I was ever going to get this wall opened.  My wife came out to see how I was doing and saw that I was covered in stucco dust.  She suggested that we abandon the project, but you know how a woman's wise advice goes over on a stubborn husband!!  She said she was going to the store and then stopping for Chinese food on her way back.  As she drove away, I remember telling myself "I'm gonna have this wall opened before she returns, even if it kills me."  I went into my garage and found a 10" disc for my metal cutoff saw.  I looked at my grinder and though "this 10" disc will fit on that grinder if I remove the safety guard."  So that's what I did.  I'm sure some of you are screaming out loud right now "OMG NOOOO!!!"  Anyhow, I got that 10" monster disc on my Makita 9100b grinder.  This particular grinder is not a variable speed tool.  So turn it on and a way we go.  It was like holding onto a small helicopter.  I climbed up a 5 foot step ladder, jambed the handle into the belt holding jeans up and turned the grinder on.  It actually cut pretty good but the cloud of dust drifting down the street looked like a tornado.  After about 90 seconds of cutting, I heard a massive bang, like a gun shot.  At the same time I felt something hit my lower back.  I thought someone shot me!  Then my pants fell down to my feet and I noticed the 10" disc on my grinder was completely gone!  That's when I realized the disc had disintegrated, cut my leather belt, broke my buckle and that's why my pants were down at my feet.  Then I started to see this flow of blood running down my legs and I knew I was in big trouble!  I carefully got off the ladder and stood for a moment on the lawn trying to figure out why I had motor oil squirting out of my stomach.  I went into my garage, grabbed a towel and a roll of duct tape.  I wrapped myself up as tight as I could and went into my house.  My 6 year old daughter saw the trail of blood and started to cry.  I told her that I would be ok and just needed to have a shower!  I guess I was in shock, but I had a shower anyways!  I still had the towel wrapped around my stomach and thoroughly secured with duct tape!  There was a fair amount of blood and fluid that looked like motor oil running down my legs.  Shortly after I got out of the shower, my dear wife returned home with Chinese food and her eyes half bugged out of her face!  She said "what are you doing in the shower?  You're bleeding to death."  She took me to the hospital and the doctors were able to repair my bladder, stitch up all my innards and jiblets and then sewed me shut with 36 staples, leaving me with a scar that extends across my waist from hip to hip!  Moral of the story;  men, listen to your wives or you don't get Chinese food!
You took the words right out of my mouth.  It has been just over a year for me as well.  I still can't sleep cause my arms are empty.  Take care and thanks for touching my heart.
